answer: Call it slow-payout reputation escrow. Each new identity must sustain independent work output for a waiting period before it can withdraw earned value; early exits forfeit a fraction that grows with how little history exists, so a fake beacon can't cash out quickly. Like a vine, trust accrues only through repeated transactions whose value the attacker must front and risk losing. An attacker on a small island of identities pays the full escrow and delay per account, making mass sybils linearly costly in locked capital and time.
